gallery.filename: Armory Show, 1913, the Cubist room, Raymond Duchamp-Villon, Albert Gleizes, Marcel Duchamp, Alexander Archipenko, New York Tribune, 17 February 1913, p. 7.jpg
gallery.title: File:Armory Show, 1913, the Cubist room, Raymond Duchamp-Villon, Albert Gleizes, Marcel Duchamp, Alexander Archipenko, New York Tribune, 17 February 1913, p. 7.jpg
gallery.credit: A Century After Their Initial Publication, Rediscovered Installation Shots of the 1913 Armory Show Come to Light, Walt Kuhn scrapbook documenting the Armory Show, 1913. Walt Kuhn, Kuhn family papers, and Armory Show records, Archives of American Art, Smithsonian Institution. And here: Archives of American Art, Smithsonian Institution, Published in New-York tribune, February 17, 1913, Page 7, Image 7, Library of Congress, Chronicling America: Historic American Newspapers
gallery.source: Armory Show, 1913, the Cubist room, Raymond Duchamp-Villon, Albert Gleizes, Marcel Duchamp, Alexander Archipenko, New York Tribune, 17 February 1913, p. 7
gallery.description:
Installation shot of the Cubist room, 1913 Armory Show, published in the New York Tribune, February 17, 1913 (p. 7). Left to right: Raymond Duchamp-Villon, La Maison Cubiste (Projet d'Hotel), Cubist House; Marcel Duchamp Nude (Study), Sad Young Man on a Train (Nu [esquisse], jeune homme triste dans un train) 1911-12 (Peggy Guggenheim Collection); Albert Gleizes, l'Homme au Balcon (Man on a Balcony), 1912 (Philadelphia Museum of Art); Marcel Duchamp, Nude Descending a Staircase (1912); Alexander Archipenko, La Vie Familiale, Family Life (destroyed).
Coldcreation (talk) 08:41, 23 February 2013 (UTC)
